newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares close weaker, market seen strong.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares close weaker, market seen strong.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares closed Friday largely weaker after a wave of profit-taking, but analysts said the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange looked generally firmer on strong investor sentiment.
"The market remains bullish, although we should see, every now and then, things softening as people take some profits, especially at the top, as happened today," one broker said.

The key 57-counter industrial index shed 8.50 points to end Friday at 10,276.12 following some losses in some bluechips, including conglomerate Delta and banking group Barclays, which lost 50 cents each to 4,400 and 3,500 respectively.

But the industrial index closed the day 163.32 points higher on the week, clocking a three-month bull run initiated mostly by local investors expecting Zimbabwe's farming-based economy to grow significantly in 1997 on the back of current good rains.
In minings, losses in gold producers Ashanti, 500 cents down at 9,500, and Rio Tinto, 100 cents lower at 2,600, pulled the secondary seven-share mining index 23.99 points down to 1,040.06.
The mining index lost 14.43 points on the week.
